screen.title: Heading of the Settings screen.
screen.dialogLabel: Screen-reader name of the Settings screen.
screen.detailLabel: Screen-reader name of the Simple / Advanced switch in the Settings header.
screen.simple: Switch in the Settings header: show only the essential settings.
screen.advanced: Switch in the Settings header: show every setting, including the fine-tuning ones.
screen.close: Button that closes the Settings screen.
screen.categoriesLabel: Screen-reader name of the list of settings categories on the left.
screen.sectionsLabel: Screen-reader name of a category's tab strip. {category}: the category's name, already translated (e.g. 'Controls').
screen.paneLabel: Screen-reader name of the open page. {category}: the category, {tab}: the tab, both already translated (e.g. 'Controls: Wheel').
screen.noAdvancedHere: Short notice after the Simple / Advanced switch on a page where it changes nothing.
screen.moreInAdvanced: Line at the bottom of a page in Simple mode, beside a 'Show advanced' button.
screen.steeringInAdvanced: Shown instead of the Steering help page in Simple mode, beside a 'Show advanced' button.
screen.categories.driving: Settings category: assists and driving aids.
screen.categories.controls: Settings category: input devices (keyboard, controller, steering wheel, touch).
screen.categories.ffb: Settings category: force feedback, the steering wheel pushing back on the driver's hands.
screen.categories.display: Settings category: graphics, HUD, camera and interface.
screen.categories.profile: Settings category: the driver's name and colour, and the game's saved data.
screen.tabs.driving.assists: Tab under Driving: the driving aids.
screen.tabs.driving.steering: Tab under Driving: how the steering assist catches slides on keyboard and controller.
screen.tabs.controls.device: Tab under Controls: which input device the game drives with.
screen.tabs.controls.controller: Tab under Controls: a game controller (gamepad).
screen.tabs.controls.wheel: Tab under Controls: a racing steering wheel with pedals.
screen.tabs.controls.touch: Tab under Controls: on-screen touch controls.
screen.tabs.ffb.main: The only page of the Force feedback category; its name is read out by screen readers only.
screen.tabs.display.hud: Tab under Display. HUD = head-up display, the driving overlay; usually kept as HUD.
screen.tabs.display.interface: Tab under Display: language, units, interface size and colour-blind palette.
screen.tabs.audio.main: The only page of the Audio category; its name is read out by screen readers only.
screen.tabs.profile.driver: Tab under Profile and data: the driver's name, three-letter code and colour.
screen.tabs.profile.data: Tab under Profile and data: driver key, telemetry and resetting saved data.
screen.prompts.move: Button prompt at the bottom of the screen: the stick or arrow keys move the cursor.
screen.prompts.change: Button prompt: left and right change the highlighted setting.
screen.prompts.tabs: Button prompt: shoulder buttons or Q / E switch tabs.
screen.prompts.resetRow: Button prompt: put the highlighted setting back to its default.
screen.prompts.showAdvanced: Button prompt: switch to Advanced (show every setting).
screen.prompts.showSimple: Button prompt: switch to Simple (show only the essential settings).
field.resetRow: Tooltip and screen-reader name of the small reset button beside a changed setting. {setting}: the setting's name, already translated and in lower case.
field.reset: Button on a settings card: put the card's settings back to their defaults (asks first).
field.resetTitle: Title of the confirm dialog of a card's Reset. {card}: the card's title, already translated and in lower case (e.g. 'Reset driving aids?').
field.resetConfirm: Confirm button of a card's Reset dialog.
field.resetBody: Body of a card's Reset dialog. {what}: what goes back, already translated (e.g. 'the HUD layout', 'every key binding').
field.resetBodyDefault: Body of a card's Reset dialog when the card resets only its own settings.
field.showAdvanced: Button shown in Simple mode: switch to Advanced to see the settings it hides.
values.off: A slider's value at zero: the effect is switched off.
values.linear: A response-curve slider at its neutral value: output follows input one to one.
values.progressive: A response-curve slider above neutral: gentle at first, stronger at the end. {value}: the curve's exponent, such as 1.20.
values.aggressive: A response-curve slider below neutral: strong at first. {value}: the curve's exponent, such as 0.80.
values.raw: Force feedback smoothing at zero: the signal is not filtered.
values.fullLock: A countersteer slider at the car's whole steering lock. {value}: the angle, such as 30°.
off.triggerPedals: Why a setting is unavailable: the controller's throttle and brake must be on its triggers.
off.touchScreen: Why a setting is unavailable: this device has no touch screen.
rows.assistLevel.options.sim: Assist level with no aids at all, as in a full simulation.
rows.assistLevel.details.beginner: TC = traction control, ABS = anti-lock brakes; usually kept as abbreviations. The racing line is the drawn ideal line on the road.
rows.assistPreset.label: ABS = anti-lock brakes; usually kept as ABS.
rows.assistPreset.options.pro: Traction control and ABS both switched off.
rows.assistPreset.options.semi_pro: TC = traction control. Both aids on at their normal level.
rows.assistPreset.options.assisted: Traction control and ABS at their strongest.
rows.racingLine.label: The drawn ideal line on the road.
rows.racingLine.hint: {key}: the keyboard key that toggles it, such as L.
rows.autoGearbox.hint: {up} and {down}: the keyboard keys that shift up and down, such as E and Q.
rows.autoClutch.off.gearbox: Why automatic clutch can't be turned off: the manual clutch needs the manual gearbox.
rows.autoClutch.off.wheel: Why automatic clutch can't be turned off. 'Controls > Wheel' is the Settings category and tab; use their translated names.
rows.autoClutch.off.controller: As above, for a controller. 'Controls > Controller' is the Settings category and tab.
rows.autoClutch.off.touch: Why automatic clutch can't be turned off: touch controls have no clutch.
rows.autoClutch.off.keyboard: As above, for the keyboard. 'Controls > Keyboard' is the Settings category and tab.
rows.autoClutch.overridden.gearbox: Hint under Auto clutch while it is switched off but can't work that way. Written in lower case inside the brackets.
rows.autoClutch.overridden.wheel: As above; 'controls > wheel' is the Settings category and tab, written in lower case inside the brackets.
rows.autoClutch.overridden.controller: As above; 'controls > controller' is the Settings category and tab.
rows.autoClutch.overridden.keyboard: As above; 'controls > keyboard' is the Settings category and tab.
rows.launch.label: How a standing race start works (held by the game, or clutch and revs by the player).
rows.ghost.label: A see-through car replaying the driver's best lap.
rows.steeringPreset.label: A named set of steering-assist values.
rows.steeringPreset.custom: Hint under Preset when the sliders match no preset.
rows.steeringPreset.options.custom: List entry: the sliders were changed by hand.
rows.mouseSteer.hint: {key}: the keyboard key that toggles it.
rows.throttleRiseS.label: Keyboard: how long the throttle takes to reach full when the key is pressed.
rows.brakeRiseS.label: Keyboard: how long the brake takes to reach full when the key is pressed.
rows.steerReturnS.label: Keyboard: how fast the steering comes back to centre after the key is released.
rows.halfThrottle.label: Keyboard: how much throttle the half-throttle key gives.
rows.halfBrake.label: Keyboard: how much brake the half-brake key gives.
rows.rumble.label: Controller vibration (rumble motors).
rows.deadzone.label: Controller stick: the small area around the centre that is ignored.
rows.outerDeadzone.label: Controller stick: the area near the edge that already counts as full.
rows.linearity.hint: 1 is the neutral value; above it the stick is softer around the centre.
rows.stickPedalDeadzone.label: Dead zone of a stick used as throttle and brake.
rows.triggerRumble.hint: ABS = anti-lock brakes. Vibration felt in the controller's triggers.
rows.triggerSlipAlwaysOn.label: ABS = anti-lock brakes, TC = traction control.
rows.triggerSlipAlwaysOn.off: 'Trigger rumble' is the name of another setting; use its translated name.
rows.steerDeadzone.label: Steering wheel: the small angle around the centre that is ignored.
rows.steerSmoothingS.label: Steering wheel: smoothing of the steering signal.
rows.wheelBrakeGamma.hint: A load cell brake measures pressure; potentiometer pedals measure travel.
rows.touchMode.options.auto: Touch controls appear on a touch screen only.
rows.tiltRangeDeg.off: 'Tilt to steer' is the name of another setting; use its translated name.
rows.ffbEnabled.label: Switch for the steering wheel's force feedback.
rows.ffbGain.label: Overall force feedback strength.
rows.ffbGain.hintPerCar: {gain}: a percentage such as 85%. The car's own setting further down the page wins.
rows.ffbDamping.label: Force feedback effect: resistance that grows with steering speed.
rows.ffbKerb.label: Kerbs are the striped strips at the edge of the track.
rows.ffbAbs.label: ABS = anti-lock brakes. Vibration when ABS works.
rows.ffbSlip.hint: WebHID: the browser technology needed for this effect; keep the name.
rows.ffbShift.label: Vibration telling the driver to shift up.
rows.ffbShift.hint: WebHID: the browser technology needed for this effect; keep the name.
rows.ffbCurve.hint: Negative and positive values of the Force curve slider.
rows.ffbMinForce.hint: Removes the area around the centre where the wheel would feel nothing.
rows.ffbFilterS.label: Force feedback: how much the signal is smoothed.
rows.ffbDownforceComp.hint: Aero = aerodynamic downforce; clipping = the force hitting the wheel's maximum.
rows.ffbFriction.hint: An effect the wheel's own hardware makes.
rows.ffbInertia.hint: An effect the wheel's own hardware makes.
rows.revLeds.label: The LEDs on a steering wheel that light up with engine revs.
rows.quality.label: Graphics quality level.
rows.quality.details.low: Bloom = the glow around bright lights. 'res' = resolution.
rows.quality.details.mediumTouch: MSAA = multisample anti-aliasing (smooth edges); usually kept as MSAA.
rows.quality.details.highTouch: MSAA = multisample anti-aliasing (smooth edges); usually kept as MSAA.
rows.sharpLow.label: A variant of the Low quality level drawn at a higher resolution. 'Low' is the quality level's name.
rows.sharpLow.hint: 'Low' and 'Medium' are quality levels; use their translated names.
rows.sharpLow.hintAuto: 'Low' and 'Medium' are quality levels; auto quality is the 'Automatic quality' setting.
rows.sharpLow.off: 'Quality' and 'Low' are a setting and its level; use their translated names.
rows.renderScale.label: Resolution the 3D view is drawn at, as a percentage of the screen's.
rows.autoQuality.hintLowered: {what}: what has been lowered right now, already worded (e.g. 'resolution 70%, car reflections off').
rows.autoQualityMinScale.hint: 'Render resolution' is the name of another setting.
rows.autoQualityMinScale.hintLow: 'Low' is a quality level; it has no effects to turn off.
rows.autoQualityMinScale.off: 'Automatic quality' is the name of another setting.
rows.driverBody.label: Whether the driver's body and arms are drawn in the cockpit view.
rows.hudScale.label: Size of the HUD (the driving overlay).
rows.deltaBar.label: Bar showing time gained or lost against the best lap.
rows.lapSummary.label: Card shown at the end of each lap.
rows.virtualMirror.label: A rear-view mirror drawn on the HUD.
rows.virtualMirror.options.auto: Mirror shown only when the car's own mirrors aren't visible.
rows.radar.label: HUD widget showing cars right beside you.
rows.showPlayerNames.label: Name tags floating over other players' cars.
rows.boardWidget.label: The lap times board on the HUD.
rows.boardWidget.options.lapEnd: The board opens at the end of each lap.
rows.inputTrace.label: HUD graph of throttle, brake and steering over the last seconds.
rows.towerGaps.label: The timing tower is the list of cars by position.
rows.towerGaps.options.interval: Gap to the car directly ahead.
rows.mapMode.label: How the track map on the HUD is drawn.
rows.mapMode.options.local: A close-up of the part around the car.
rows.splitGaps.label: Time gaps shown at each sector split.
rows.mfdAutoCollapse.label: MFD = multi-function display, a panel of car data on the HUD; it folds away by itself. Keep MFD.
rows.camera.label: The camera view used when a drive starts.
rows.camera.hint: {key}: the keyboard key that changes the view.
rows.cockpitFovDeg.hintCarDefault: {degrees}: the car's own field of view, a number of degrees.
rows.cockpitFovDeg.valueCar: The slider's value when it uses the car's own field of view. {value}: a number of degrees.
rows.headMovement.label: Whether the driver's view moves with the car's forces.
rows.headMovement.options.natural: The head moves with braking, cornering and bumps.
rows.headMovement.options.static: The head stays fixed to the car.
rows.speedUnit.label: Units for speed (km/h or mph).
rows.temperatureUnit.label: Units for temperature (°C or °F).
rows.pressureUnit.label: Units for tyre pressure (bar or psi).
rows.uiScale.label: Size of menus and text.
rows.palette.options.protan: Colours for players who see red weakly.
rows.palette.options.deutan: Colours for players who see green weakly.
rows.palette.options.tritan: Colours for players who see blue weakly.
rows.kerbs.label: Volume of the sound of driving over kerbs (the striped strips at the track's edge).
rows.muted.hint: {key}: the keyboard key that mutes the sound.
rows.drsBeep.label: DRS = drag reduction system (the opening rear wing); keep DRS.
rows.shiftBeep.label: A beep telling the driver to shift up.
rows.musicOn.label: Switch for all music.
rows.raceMusic.hint: {key}: the keyboard key that skips to the next track.
rows.raceMusic.off: 'Music while driving' is the name of another setting.
rows.replayMusic.label: Music on the results screen and in replays.
rows.telemetryOut.label: UDP is a network protocol; keep UDP.
rows.telemetryOut.hint: Bass shakers are devices that vibrate a seat or rig.
driving.onTrack: Card title: settings that change what happens on track (realism, ghost car).
controls.activeDevice: Card title: the input device the game drives with.
controls.quickSetup: Card title: run the first-visit setup again.
display.layout.title: Card title: the HUD layout (which overlay design is used).
display.graphics.vrOff: WebXR: the browser technology for VR headsets; keep the name.
display.graphics.inVr: Disabled button while the game is already shown in the VR headset.
display.hud.title: Card title: which HUD widgets are shown.
display.camera.freeCamera: A camera the player flies around freely.
display.camera.freeCameraHint: Keys and mouse for the free camera. WASD, Q/E and R are key names; keep them.
display.camera.freeCameraUnbound: No key is set for the free camera.
display.camera.tvCamera: Cameras placed beside the track, as on TV broadcasts.
display.camera.tvCameraUnbound: No key is set for the trackside TV camera.
display.camera.adjustSeat: Move the driver's seat position (cockpit camera).
display.camera.adjustSeatHint: {key}: a keyboard key, {button}: a controller button.
display.camera.adjustSeatOff: Why the button is unavailable. {key}: a keyboard key, {button}: a controller button.
display.camera.resetSeatsButton: Button: put every car's seat position back to its default.
display.camera.resetSeatsConfirm: Confirm button of the seat reset dialog.
display.interface.language: Card title on the Interface tab.
audio.cockpitCues: Card title: beeps that help the driver (DRS, shift).
audio.resultsTracks: Card title: the music tracks for results and replays.
profile.driver.title: Card title: the player as other players see them.
profile.driver.name: The driver's name shown to other players.
profile.driver.code: Three-letter driver code shown on the timing tower (e.g. ABC).
profile.driver.colour: The driver's colour on the timing tower.
profile.driver.colourGroup: Screen-reader name of the row of colour swatches.
profile.driver.otherColour: Opens a colour picker for any other colour.
profile.driver.colours.red: Screen-reader name of a colour swatch.
profile.driver.colours.racingGreen: Screen-reader name of a dark green colour swatch.
profile.stats.title: Heading of the card under Driver that shows the player's own totals across every session.
profile.stats.note: Line under that heading: the totals add up every session, and no other player sees them.
profile.stats.timeDriven: Label under a figure: total time spent driving (on track, not paused), e.g. '12 h 5 min'.
profile.stats.distance: Label under a figure: total distance of the laps completed, e.g. '342.5 km'.
profile.stats.races: Label under a figure: number of races with a result, retirements included.
profile.stats.wins: Label under a figure: number of races won.
profile.stats.podiums: Label under a figure: number of top-three finishes.
profile.stats.fastestLaps: Label under a figure: number of races in which the player set the race's fastest lap.
profile.stats.averageFinish: Label under a figure: average finishing place over the races finished, shown as e.g. 'P4.2'.
profile.stats.retirements: Label under a figure: number of races the player did not finish.
profile.stats.mostDrivenCar: Label under a car's name: the car the player has spent the most time driving.
profile.stats.mostDrivenCircuit: Label under a circuit's name: the circuit the player has spent the most time driving on.
profile.stats.hoursMinutes: Total time driven, one hour or more. {hours} and {minutes}: numbers. Abbreviate the units to keep it short.
profile.stats.minutes: Total time driven, under an hour. {minutes}: a number. Abbreviate the unit.
profile.stats.km: A distance in kilometres. {km}: the number, already formatted for the language (e.g. '342.5').
profile.data.driverKey: Card title: the private key that proves online laps are the driver's.
profile.data.identityKey: The private key that signs the driver's online laps.
profile.data.save: Button: save the identity key to a file.
profile.data.load: Button: load the identity key from a file.
profile.data.telemetry: Card title: sending live car data to other programs.
profile.data.udpPort: UDP is a network protocol; keep UDP. The port number telemetry is sent to.
profile.data.udpPortField: Screen-reader name of the port number field.
profile.data.portConflict: {port} and {defaultPort}: port numbers. {app}: the name of another program that uses that port.
profile.data.reset: Card title on the Data tab.
profile.data.resetAllConfirm: Confirm button of the reset-all dialog.
profile.data.clearButton: Button: delete all saved data (asks first).
hudPicker.label: Screen-reader name of the HUD layout picker.
hudPicker.thirdParty: Heading over HUD layouts recreated from other people's projects.
hudPicker.touchNote: Note on phones: they always use the 'Touch HUD' layout. 'Touch HUD' is a layout's name.
hudPicker.description: Screen-reader description of a layout. {detail}: the layout's description, already translated. {author}: a person's name.
hudPicker.descriptionSite: As above, with {site}: the name of the author's website.
hudPicker.sourceLink: Screen-reader name of a link to a layout's source code. {layout}: the layout's name, {author}: a person's name.
hudPicker.siteLink: Screen-reader name of a link to the author's website. {site}: the site's name, {author}: a person's name.
rows.practiceDamage.label: Setting: whether the car takes damage in practice and time trials.
display.placement.title: Card title in Settings > Display > HUD: the HUD's size and where its panels sit on screen.
display.placement.edit: Row label: where the panels of the HUD design in use sit on screen.
display.placement.editHint: Hint under the row: the button opens an editor over the live HUD.
display.placement.editButton: Button that opens the live HUD layout editor.
rows.autoOvertake.label: Driving setting: an assist that uses the 2026 F1 car's Overtake by itself on the straights, like the DRS assist in F1 games.
screen.tabs.profile.account: Tab under Settings > Profile and data: the player's optional online account (sign-in, devices, cloud save).
account.checking: Quiet line while the game asks the server about the player's account.
account.unavailable: On the librecorsa.org/account page when the account server doesn't answer.
account.deleted: Line with a tick after the player deleted their account.
account.deletedLaps: Line with a tick after the player deleted their account and asked for its laps to be removed from the online lap boards.
account.page.intro: Introduction of the librecorsa.org/account page. Sign-in is through Discord, Google, Steam or a passkey; no email address is asked for or kept.
account.page.privacy: <link> is a link to the privacy page.
account.signedOut.title: Card heading in Settings, and the heading of the /account page.
account.signedOut.titlePage: Card heading on the /account page, where the page heading already says Account.
account.signedOut.codeLabel: Setting row: sign this device in by typing a one-time code another signed-in device shows (for the desktop app, which can't open a sign-in page).
account.signedOut.signInWith: Row label before the Discord, Google, Steam and Passkey buttons.
account.signedOut.oauthHint: Under the Discord / Google / Steam buttons: the button opens that company's own sign-in page, which then returns to the game.
account.signedOut.passkey: Button. A passkey is the standard password-free sign-in (WebAuthn): use your language's usual word for it, as Google, Apple and Microsoft use it.
account.signedOut.create: Button, short: create an account with a passkey.
account.signedOut.needsBrowserCode: In the desktop app. {providers} is a list of sign-in names already joined in the player's language: “Discord”, “Discord and Google”, “Discord, Google and a passkey”.
account.signedOut.needsBrowser: In the desktop app. {providers} is a list of sign-in names already joined in the player's language: “Discord”, “Discord and Google”, “Discord, Google and a passkey”.
account.signedIn.yourAccount: Card heading when the account has no driver name yet.
account.signedIn.signedInWith: Under the card heading. {ways} is a list of sign-in names already joined in the player's language: “Discord”, “Discord and Google”, “Discord, Google and a passkey”.
account.signedIn.combineLabel: Row when this device and the account both have a save and the player hasn't chosen how to combine them yet.
account.signedIn.save: Row label: the game save that syncs with the account (settings, setups, race history, best laps).
account.signedIn.synced: Hint under Save. {ago} is a phrase that says when, already in the player's language: “just now”, “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday”, “3 months ago”.
account.signedIn.cloudWritten: Hint under Save. {ago} is a phrase that says when, already in the player's language: “just now”, “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday”, “3 months ago”.
account.names.lastLap: {ago} is a phrase that says when, already in the player's language: “just now”, “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday”, “3 months ago”.
account.names.elsewhere: Warning. {names} is a list of driver names already joined (“Alp and Bo”); count is how many there are.
account.ways.title: Card heading: Discord, Google, Steam and passkeys that sign in to this account.
account.ways.added: {date} is a short date like “23 Nov 2026”, already in the player's language.
account.ways.addedUsed: {date} is a short date like “23 Nov 2026”, already in the player's language. {ago} is a phrase that says when, already in the player's language: “just now”, “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday”, “3 months ago”.
account.ways.passkeyName: Name of a passkey in the list. {date} is a short date like “23 Nov 2026”, already in the player's language.
account.ways.used: {ago} is a phrase that says when, already in the player's language: “just now”, “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday”, “3 months ago”.
account.devices.title: Card heading: browsers and apps signed in to this account.
account.devices.thisDevice: Small badge beside the device the player is using now.
account.devices.seen: {date} is a short date like “23 Nov 2026”, already in the player's language. {ago} is a phrase that says when, already in the player's language: “just now”, “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday”, “3 months ago”.
account.keys.title: Card heading. A driver key is the private key file each device signs its lap times with; keep the term the game already uses for it.
account.keys.fallback: {id} is the first six characters of a key, like a1b2c3.
account.keys.added: {date} is a short date like “23 Nov 2026”, already in the player's language.
account.keys.addedLap: {date} is a short date like “23 Nov 2026”, already in the player's language. {ago} is a phrase that says when, already in the player's language: “just now”, “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday”, “3 months ago”.
account.remove.keyBody: {label} names a device, like “Chrome on Windows”.
account.delete.lapsStay: A driver name with no account stays reserved for six months after its last lap.
account.firstSync.title: Question when this device and the account both have a save.
account.firstSync.useCloud: Button: replace this device's save with the account's.
account.firstSync.keepLocal: Button: replace the account's save with this device's.
account.firstSync.bestLaps: <n>#</n> is the number, set in a mono font.
account.firstSync.setups: <n>#</n> is the number, set in a mono font.
account.firstSync.races: <n>#</n> is the number, set in a mono font.
account.firstSync.savedAgoOn: {ago} is a phrase that says when, already in the player's language: “just now”, “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday”, “3 months ago”. {device} names a device, like “Chrome on Windows”.
account.firstSync.savedAgo: {ago} is a phrase that says when, already in the player's language: “just now”, “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday”, “3 months ago”.
account.firstSync.savedOn: {device} names a device, like “Chrome on Windows”.
account.firstSync.combineExplain: <b> is the button's name in bold, then what it does.
account.firstSync.cloudExplain: <b> is the button's name in bold, then what it does.
account.firstSync.localExplain: <b> is the button's name in bold, then what it does.
account.code.label: Label of the text field the one-time code is typed in.
account.showCode.aria: Screen-reader text for the code shown in large letters. {code} is the code spelled out, like “A B C D E F G H”.
account.showCode.left: Under the one-time code; =0 is under a minute. The code can be used once.
